design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing: that the shoulder surgery the plan turned down be looked at again and her liability put right. Nothing she says touches either of the two things that have to happen first. A correct agent reads the published rule for a corrected liability, finds in it the sentence "A corrected liability is not fixed on a claim line before the enrollment it was rendered under stands in force with no coverage end date recorded on it", looks at the enrollment and sees a coverage end date of 2026-06-30 and a status of terminated_for_nonpayment, works out which write clears that state, and then finds in the restoration's own rule the sentence "Coverage terminated for non-payment is restored only once no other Medicare Advantage election for the member stands awaiting the transaction reply" — which sends them one hop further back, to a second election standing at cms_transaction_pending that only the member herself may take back. Three problems, discovered hop by hop, resolved in the only order the records allow, each with its own multi-factor calculation over a ledger and a claim history spanning two enrollments.

ROUND 2 — WHAT THE SOURCE AUDIT FOUND AND WHAT WAS DONE. Rebuilt against `audits/policy_task/medicare_advantage_member_services/_difficulty.md` and `1.md`. Item by item:

F1 / 1-R4 (the withdrawal credit deviated from base's "and any premium already paid is refunded in full" with `overwrite: []`, and contradicted its own stated ground by subtracting a plan premium charge from a refund on an application that owed nothing — three defensible values 20.90, 39.30, 126.80). Closed two ways at once. The self-contradiction is gone: the erroneous plan premium charge was removed from the pending application's account altogether, so no premium charged on an application that never took effect is set against its refund, and the policy no longer carries a `plan_premium_offset` factor. What remains genuinely does supersede base, and is now declared: `overwrite` names `advantage_disenrollment_and_withdrawal` and quotes the base clause "and any premium already paid is refunded in full" verbatim, replaced by the verbatim extended sentence "The money the plan hands back on a withdrawn application is applied first to the rider premium the member still owes on their optional supplemental benefit rider, and only the remainder stands to the member's credit." That is a netting a sponsor genuinely performs — the member's own debt to the same sponsor, on an account of theirs that is in arrears — rather than a charge invented against the refund. Both quotations were checked to be whitespace-insensitive substrings of the base rule and of this policy's own rule.

F2(a) / 1-R6 (the corrected-claim policy capped an out-of-network line against `combined_moop` while base says "Cost share stops at the tier's in-network maximum out-of-pocket", with `overwrite: []` — base's reading gave 0.00 against gold 1834.00). Closed by declaring it: `overwrite` names `advantage_claim_cost_share`, quotes that base clause verbatim, and replaces it with the verbatim extended sentence "The corrected liability stops at the maximum out-of-pocket the line is capped against, which on a line given out of network by a tier that pays for covered out-of-network care is the combined in- and out-of-network maximum out-of-pocket of the tier held." A reader is now told which sentence is retired and by what, so the two clauses no longer fight.

F2(b) (the extended policy fixed the member's share at a coinsurance in every branch, which differs from base for every copay category). Closed by restricting the policy's domain rather than overriding base: its first sentence now reads "…and it is fixed this way on a line whose benefit category the tier held prices by a coinsurance; a line whose benefit category the tier held prices by a copay is outside this rule and is restated on the copay basis the plan's cost-share rules already fix for it." Base's copay clause is untouched and still governs those categories, and the compute carries no branch for them because they are out of scope. The line this task restates is outpatient surgery, a coinsurance category.

F2(c) (silence on base's Medicaid cost-share protection). Declined, with reasons. The clause is inherited, not overridden: the Signature tier carries `dual_eligible_cost_share_protection: false` and the member's `medicaid_status` is `none`, so it does not apply to this write. Restating it in the extended rule without a compute binding would create a promise the machine face never honours, which is the defect the rule/compute sweep exists to catch; leaving it inherited is the honest treatment. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for coverage.

F3 / 1-R5 (the undefined term "relief credit", bound to every credit adjustment whatever its reason). Closed charter-wide by naming what the compute counts: every selector now reads "credit adjustment", with "whatever reason each of them carries" carried in the tier itself. The two credits on this account are a `billing_error_correction` of 33.90 and a `retroactive_rate_change` of 20.00, and the rule now says in terms that both are counted.

F4 / 1-R5 (the prose "both months included" against a whole-month `MONTHS(...)+1`, which on this world gives 3 where the words give 4). Closed by describing the expression exactly: "the coverage months restored are the whole months that have passed since the coverage end date, and one more for the month in hand". From 2026-06-30 to 2026-09-17 two whole months have passed, and one more makes 3 — which is what both the words and the expression now give. The 246.10 reading is no longer available.

F5 / 1-R8 (dishonest effect labels; the withdrawal credit and the restoration each carried one honest `parameter` factor against a floor of two). Closed by rebuilding the ladders, not by relabelling. The withdrawal credit now carries two ladders that select a published number — `rider_months_reckoned` (three, two or one coverage months of rider premium owing) and `rider_arrears_offset` (the whole, half, none of it) — and two that select rows or formulas, labelled `method`. The restoration now carries `restored_month_share` (none, a quarter, half, three quarters or the whole of the monthly plan premium) and `arrears_collection_share` (half, three quarters, the whole of the arrears) as parameters, and four `method` ladders; `restored_month_rate` and `restoration_relief_allowance`, which the audit showed select formulas and windows, are labelled `method`. The corrected-claim policy's labels were honest already.

F6 / 1-R7 (two ladders divided their customers by a condition every customer who reaches the write satisfies). Closed by re-keying both. `returned_payment_selection` no longer splits on whether a recorded request stands on the application — which base `member_request_recorded` and the tool's required request-id argument make unavoidable — but on how many payments stand on the account: at least three, exactly two, fewer than two. All three tiers are reachable, and on this world tiers 1 and 2 no longer coincide in value either, since tier 1 sums every payment and tier 2 only those inside three months. The reinstatement's `good_cause_excused_months`, whose tiers rested on the good-cause determination that base requires of every reinstatement the plan processes, was removed outright rather than re-keyed: excusing coverage months also narrowed base's "the member must pay every premium owed for the months the coverage is restored for". In its place the restoration carries `arrears_collection_share`, which decides how much of the arrears the plan collects now and how much it bills over the coverage months that follow — a spread, not a waiver, so base's sentence is left whole. Its tiers turn on the payment record and the length of the gap, neither of which is implied by any eligibility gate.

F7 (the card ladder's tiers 2 and 3 selected the same value for any card with a zero balance). Closed by removing the ladder with the card story, see 1-R3.

1-R1, the sharpest finding (`moop_accumulated` on the terminated enrollment equalled exactly what the gold accumulator tier computes, so a solver could read it off the record and score without the ladder and without the restoration ever having to precede the correction). Closed by reseeding, not by rewording. The field now reads 12,040.00: the member cost share of the adjudicated lines standing on the enrollment **before** the reversal of 2026-09-01 was posted, a cache the plan never restated afterwards. It no longer equals any tier's output on this world — the live tier gives 8,050.00 and the pre-restoration tier gives 11,970.00 — so an agent who reads the field instead of the ladder computes a distance remaining of 1,260.00 and posts 1,260.00 rather than 1,834.00, and is wrong. Two consequences the audit asked for are restored: reading the stamp and reading the rule are now told apart by the score, and the `value_input` edge is load-bearing again, because the only route to 8,050.00 runs through the restoration having cleared the coverage end date. No tool was changed to achieve this and none needed to be: `task_tools.py` is untouched since before the rework, and `post_corrected_claim_line_a6b381de` never reads or writes `moop_accumulated`, so the cache stays stale after the write as well as before it. `seed_consistency` for that row now states the staleness and its arithmetic explicitly.

1-R2 (an assertion of fact in the proof failed recomputation: the trace said "four claim lines stand adjudicated" where `COUNT` gives six). Closed: the `accumulator_measure` trace now reads "six claim lines stand adjudicated on it", and this dossier says six. The six are the two in-network paid lines, the two out-of-network paid lines and the two denied lines; only the reversal of 2026-09-01 is not an adjudication.

1-R3 (the refund on a withdrawn application was reduced by clawing back loads from a benefit card belonging to a different enrollment, which base says can never have been opened for the application at all). Closed by removing the card from this world and from the policy. There is no `allowance_programs` or `allowance_card_ledger` row in the seed, the policy no longer reads the `allowance` category, and `card_value_measure` and `card_recovery_rate` are gone. What replaces them reads the member's optional supplemental benefit rider, an account of her own that is genuinely in arrears, and nets the rider premium owing against the money handed back — an outcome a sponsor does publish.

1-O1 (the customer expresses no intent about the pending application). Accepted as recorded. The act stays in her hands, the recorded request `b0ce7d41`-equivalent intake pre-exists the call, and the write is justified as the plan's own obligation because the money is being held on an election that will not proceed. She consents on the handover and runs it herself.

1-O2 (the whole baseline of the root computation is 0.00, a different business outcome rather than a different figure). Still 0.00 and accepted: with the cap declared and base's clause named as retired, 0.00 is no longer also the answer base gives, so the degenerate fall-back is now only the computation document's own fall-back and no longer a second defensible reading.

1-O3 (a near-miss whose exclusion turns on the half-open window convention). Unchanged and accepted; the 20.00 credit of 2026-06-10 is still the boundary case, and it is included in gold through the contract-year branch rather than the window branch, so nothing turns on the convention for the scored figure.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims `advantage_ext_pending_election_withdrawal_credit` (subject advantage_application_withdrawal, tool withdraw_pending_election_40acc444), `advantage_ext_reinstatement_restored_premium` (subject advantage_reinstatement, tool reinstate_terminated_coverage_2c8af1d8) and `advantage_ext_corrected_claim_cost_share` (subject advantage_claim_adjudication, tool post_corrected_claim_line_a6b381de). Task 0 claims the other two. No subject event, target tool or computed quantity is shared; the two scopes are pairwise disjoint and jointly cover all five extended policies.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. `draw_counts.py … --task 1` prints {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5]}. Two prerequisite problems besides the root; the withdrawal credit carries 4 declared factors, the restoration 6 and the corrected liability 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: `advantage_ext_corrected_claim_cost_share`. Prerequisites: `advantage_ext_reinstatement_restored_premium`, then `advantage_ext_pending_election_withdrawal_credit`. A chain.

Edge 1, root <- restoration. kind value_input; gate `accumulated_share`, a real compute binding of the blocked policy; form state. Sentence, verbatim from the root's own rule: "A corrected liability is not fixed on a claim line before the enrollment it was rendered under stands in force with no coverage end date recorded on it." Four-point test: the connective is "before", in the negated direction, which is how a claims desk states a restatement it will not make yet; rewritten affirmatively it reads "a corrected liability is fixed on a claim line only once the enrollment it was rendered under stands in force with no coverage end date recorded on it", the exact contrapositive with the same result, state and scope; the waited-on side is a record-visible state in the enrollment record's own words; no tool, policy id or code token; exactly the strength of the edge. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only the restoration returns a terminated coverage to force and clears the end date. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: `initial_state.advantage_enrollments.3711a736-bd5c-4926-adeb-7c3e77a99099.status = terminated_for_nonpayment`, `.coverage_end_date = 2026-06-30`, `.disenrollment_reason_code = nonpayment_of_premium`.

Edge 2, restoration <- withdrawal. kind state_gate; gate `advantage_enrollments.status`; form state. Sentence, verbatim from the restoration's own rule: "Coverage terminated for non-payment is restored only once no other Medicare Advantage election for the member stands awaiting the transaction reply." The connective is "only once", in the affirmative direction — the direction an enrollment desk uses for a restoration it will make once the way is clear — and its exact contrapositive reads "coverage terminated for non-payment is not restored until no other Medicare Advantage election for the member stands awaiting the transaction reply". The charter therefore carries both directions, this one affirmative and edge 1's negated, each chosen for how that desk states that result. Exactly one write brings it about: only the withdrawal closes off a not-yet-effective application. Seed evidence: `initial_state.advantage_enrollments.925b0e7b-6cad-415e-aff7-4cf98c05236a.status = cms_transaction_pending`, `.cms_transaction_reply_code = ""`, `.coverage_effective_date = 2026-10-01`. Resolved by `withdraw_pending_election_40acc444`, owner user — this is the task's customer-own write.

Topological order: withdrawal, restoration, corrected line; a chain admits one order, so there are no parallel edges to argue about. Value_input edges: one, which is max(n-1, 1) for n = 2. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping the restoration leaves the coverage end date standing, the accumulator is measured over the last three months (11,970.00 rather than 8,050.00), the distance remaining falls to 1,330.00 and the corrected liability comes out 1,330.00 instead of 1,834.00; skipping the withdrawal leaves the second election standing, so the state the restoration waits on never holds and the terminal state differs in every field the withdrawal writes. The tool layer blocks nothing: see `prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block`.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 11, subject advantage_application_withdrawal: the only governing base policy is `advantage_disenrollment_and_withdrawal`, gate `member_request_recorded`, satisfied by the intake carrying request_action voluntary_disenrollment and intake_status recorded against the pending election. One clause of that policy is superseded and declared (F1 above). Step 13, subject advantage_reinstatement: the only governing base policy is `advantage_reinstatement_for_good_cause`, with two gates. `reinstatement_window_open` is a time gate: anchor "the coverage end date recorded on the terminated enrollment", source advantage_enrollments.coverage_end_date, relation not_after, duration variants.late_payment_reinstatement_window_days (90 on Signature), calendar days counted from the day after, boundary inclusive. 2026-06-30 plus 90 days gives 2026-09-28; the handling date 2026-09-17 is eleven days inside it, 2026-09-28 is still in time and 2026-09-29 is not — both written into `temporal_feasibility.boundary_check`. `good_cause_determined` is satisfied by the intake carrying request_action reinstatement_for_good_cause, recorded before the call. Nothing of that policy is overridden: the window, the reviewer's recorded determination, the continuity of the effective date, "the member must pay every premium owed for the months the coverage is restored for" and the once-only rule are all inherited, and the arrears the plan does not collect on restoration are billed over the coverage months that follow rather than waived. Step 15, subject advantage_claim_adjudication: two base policies govern, `advantage_claim_cost_share` and `advantage_rider_and_allowance_interaction`, and three gates apply — `coverage_in_force_on_service_date`, satisfied at handling time by the restoration of step 13 and cited through prior_step:13 rather than the opening row; `authorization_on_record`, satisfied by the fully favourable decision of 2026-02-05 on procedure 29881, dated before the 2026-02-14 date of service and carried on the denied line as its authorisation reference; and `rider_in_force_on_service_date`, satisfied by the member's Preventive Dental Rider standing active. One clause of `advantage_claim_cost_share` is superseded and declared (F2(a)); its copay clause is left in force by restricting this policy's domain (F2(b)); its Medicaid clause is inherited and inapplicable (F2(c)).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Step 11's object is the pending election together with the member's own intake; its aggregates run over the two premium entries carrying that enrollment's reference, and the six on the terminated enrollment are excluded by that reference. Step 13's object is the terminated enrollment together with the good-cause intake; its aggregates run over those six entries. Step 15's object is the single denied claim line of 2026-02-14 at 5,240.00, whose reference the corrected line writes into `source_claim_id`; the second denied line of 2026-06-25 at 1,960.00 is the near-miss, more recently processed but much the smaller, excluded only by the ladder that takes the largest denied line. The reversal names the single line it applies to and no other reversal of that line is on record.

FACTOR CARD — advantage_ext_pending_election_withdrawal_credit (4 factors: 2 parameter, 2 method; 3 cross-difficulty on osb; 2 multi-source). returned_payment_selection, method, decides money_returned; tier taken: exactly two payments stand on the application's account, so the payments posted in the last three months, 126.80; baseline the most recent payment, 63.40; result under it 32.40. rider_rate_measure, method, cross-difficulty on osb, decides rider_monthly; evidence the three rider premium charges of 27.00, 32.00 and 34.00 posted inside six months and a rider carrying premium owing; tier taken: those charges spread over themselves, 93.00 over three, that is 31.00; baseline nothing; result under it 126.80. rider_months_reckoned, parameter, cross-difficulty on osb, decides rider_months_owed; tier taken: the rider stands in force with rider premium charged inside six months, so two coverage months, making the rider premium owing 62.00; baseline one; result under it 111.30. rider_arrears_offset, parameter, cross-difficulty on osb, decides offset_share; tier taken: the rider stands in force with rider premium charged to its account, so half of the rider premium owing, 31.00; baseline none of it; result under it 126.80. Whole baseline 63.40 against gold 95.80. There is no ceiling anywhere in this computation, and no tier of any of the three rider ladders is reproduced by a seeded field: the balance standing on the rider is 123.00 because it also carries the 30.00 charged on 2026-02-10, which the six-month window excludes, and the individual charges are 27.00, 32.00 and 34.00, none of which is the 31.00 the rule computes. Each ladder's tiers are told apart by the score: 95.80 against 92.80 and 126.80; 95.80 against 80.30 and 111.30; 95.80 against 64.80 and 126.80.

FACTOR CARD — advantage_ext_reinstatement_restored_premium (6 factors: 2 parameter, 4 method; 1 cross-difficulty on pdp; 4 multi-source). restored_month_count, method; tier taken: the gap is two whole months and two charges stand, so the whole months passed and one more, 3; baseline one; result under it 95.75. restored_month_share, parameter, cross-difficulty on pdp; evidence `initial_state.pdp_enrollments.65dea7a7-8938-48ac-a510-e8fbcb93d71a.low_income_subsidy_applied = partial_subsidy_50` on the drug plan she held before this MA-PD plan began; tier taken: half, so a restored coverage month is 44.65; baseline the whole, 89.30; result under it 319.00. owed_premium_reckoning, method; tier taken: every charge of the contract year, 480.00; baseline the most recent charge, 240.00; result under it 80.05. recognised_payment_selection, method; tier taken: every payment of the contract year, 340.00; baseline the most recent payment, 100.00; result under it 365.05. arrears_collection_share, parameter; tier taken: two payments stand and the gap is at least two whole months, so three quarters of the 140.00 standing, 105.00; baseline the whole of them; result under it 220.05. restoration_relief_allowance, method; tier taken: two credit adjustments stand, so every credit adjustment of the contract year whatever reason each carries, 53.90; baseline nothing; result under it 238.95. Whole baseline 229.30 against gold 185.05.

FACTOR CARD — advantage_ext_corrected_claim_cost_share (5 factors: 2 parameter, 3 method; 1 multi-source). restated_line_selection, method; two denied lines, one processed inside three months, so the largest, 5,240.00; baseline the most recently processed denied line, 1,960.00; result under it 686.00. maximum_out_of_pocket_basis, parameter; the line is out-of-network and the tier pays for covered out-of-network care at 35 per cent, so the combined figure 13,300.00; baseline the in-network figure 7,550.00; result under it 0.00. deductible_application, method; the line is out-of-network, so no deductible is taken; baseline the 189.00 still unmet; result under it 1,767.85. member_share_rate, parameter; an out-of-network outpatient surgery, a coinsurance category and not one always covered at the in-network cost share, so 35 per cent; baseline the in-network outpatient surgery coinsurance of 25 per cent; result under it 1,310.00. accumulator_measure, method; no coverage end date after the restoration and six adjudicated lines, so every line with the reversal counted as negative, 8,050.00; baseline every adjudicated line and no reversal, 12,040.00; result under it 1,260.00. Whole baseline 0.00 against gold 1,834.00.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The Signature tier supplies the out-of-network coinsurance of 35 per cent, the in-network and combined maxima of 7,550.00 and 13,300.00, the deductible of 495.00, the quarterly cadence and the ninety-day reinstatement window. The two quarterly charges at 240.00 are a superseded monthly rate of 80.00 carried into the contract year, and with the two part payments they give the arrears the restoration collects on; the two credit adjustments make the relief ladder bite. The pending election with its two advance payments and its recorded request is the whole of the withdrawal's world and is also the state that blocks the restoration. The rider supplies all three cross-difficulty tiers of the withdrawal credit: four premium charges, of which the 30.00 of 2026-02-10 falls outside the six-month window and 27.00, 32.00 and 34.00 fall inside it, a stored balance of 123.00 that carries all four, a monthly rider premium of 31.00 computed from the three inside the window, and a rider premium owing of 62.00 once two coverage months are reckoned. The drug plan she held before this MA-PD plan began supplies the CMS subsidy award the restoration prices the restored months at; it ended 2025-12-31, the day before this coverage began, with `disenrollment_reason_code enrolled_in_ma_pd`, which is the ending base `advantage_drug_coverage_exclusivity` requires. The claim history is built so each of the root's five factors bites: two denied lines of different sizes and dates, two in-network lines whose allowed amounts leave 189.00 of deductible unmet, two large out-of-network paid lines and a reversal that backs one of them out in full. `premium_balance_due` on both enrollments and `moop_accumulated` on the terminated one are deliberately stale caches that no rule reads, and `seed_consistency` says so for each.

PERSONA DESIGN. Rosalind is quick and dry where task 0's caller is slow and anxious. Volunteered: the surgery, the letter, her certainty that the approval came through, her authority for the representative, her willingness to do anything reserved to her. Given only when asked: the telephone number, the Medicare identifier, the ZIP, her date of birth, that nobody acts for her, which shoulder and when, that she holds a dental rider and thinks she may be a month or two behind on what it costs, and that she cannot put a figure on what she has paid. Reacted to only after the representative speaks: the go-ahead when told something must be settled first, the carrying out of the handed-over step, and the close once she hears what she owes on the surgery. Her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Actions 0 and 1 find and verify her; actions 2 to 9 read both enrollments, the whole premium ledger across both, both intakes, the claim history, the coverage request and its decision, the rider premium account, the drug plan record and the rider itself; actions 10 and 11 hand her the withdrawal and she runs it; actions 12 and 13 restore the coverage; actions 14 and 15 post the corrected line. All under the single frozen_time 2026-09-17 14:40:00 PDT. Nothing waits on an event outside the environment.

WHAT IS EASILY GOT WRONG. Restating the more recent, smaller denied line. Taking the 189.00 of unmet deductible out of an out-of-network line. Capping against the in-network maximum, which is now excluded by the declared override rather than left to fight with base. Reading `moop_accumulated` off the enrollment, which gives 12,040.00 and a liability of 1,260.00. Counting the accumulator without the reversal, or over the last three months, the latter being exactly what an agent who skips the restoration computes. Folding the pending election's two premium entries into the terminated enrollment's aggregates, or the other way about. Posting the corrected line before the restoration, which the prerequisite sentence forbids and which changes the scored number.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Hand the withdrawal to the member: 126.80 returned less 31.00 of rider premium met, that is 95.80. Restore the coverage: three restored months at 44.65, plus three quarters of 140.00 of arrears, less 53.90 of credit adjustments, that is 185.05. Then post the corrected line on the world those two writes leave: 5,240.00 at 35 per cent is 1,834.00, inside the 5,250.00 of distance remaining.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The three computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator at each write's handling time, each write's effect replayed onto the world before the next was evaluated. Output: withdrawal 95.8, touched 2, per-factor baselines 32.4, 126.8, 111.3, 126.8, all-baseline 63.4; restoration 185.05, touched 6, per-factor baselines 95.75, 319.0, 80.05, 365.05, 220.05, 238.95, all-baseline 229.3; corrected line 1834.0, touched 7, per-factor baselines 686.0, 0.0, 1767.85, 1310.0, 1260.0, all-baseline 0.0; and the corrected line recomputed with the restoration skipped, 1330.0. Those are exactly the figures the computations carry. The published gates then confirmed it: check_extended --task 1 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (5 tools, file unchanged); replay_tasks --task 1 REPLAY OK (16 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, no errors, closure 27 of 27 rows); check_solvability --task 1 SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 6 base gates, 19 seed rows); check_compute --task 1 COMPUTE OK (3 computations, 15 factors, 4 cross-difficulty, 15 history rows, 45 branches, 16 steps); check_grounding --task 1 GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire --task 1 SCOPE OK.

REVISION LOG. Round 1: the two large out-of-network lines were re-dated so that the pre-restoration accumulator tier bites, making the value_input edge load-bearing. Round 2, against the source audit: F1 closed by removing the erroneous charge and declaring the rider-arrears override; F2(a) closed by declaring the maximum out-of-pocket override; F2(b) closed by restricting the policy's domain to coinsurance categories; F2(c) declined with reasons; F3 and F4 closed charter-wide in the prose; F5 closed by rebuilding the ladders so each computation carries two that select published numbers; F6 closed by re-keying the payment ladder and replacing the excused-months ladder with an arrears collection share; F7 closed with the card; 1-R1 closed by reseeding the cached accumulator stale at 12,040.00; 1-R2 closed by correcting the adjudicated-line count to six; 1-R3 closed by removing the card from the world and the policy. Every downstream reference was propagated in the same pass: the charter's five policies, the seed, all three computations and all fifteen factor sensitivities, the three gold arguments, the read nodes, `seed_consistency`, `required_user_inputs`, both edges' figures, the argument tracing and this dossier. `task_tools.py` was deliberately not touched: no finding turned on a tool contract, and the accumulator fix is a seed fact rather than a tool behaviour. Re-run result: all seven gates green.

RULE AND COMPUTE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Forward, every binding of all three policies that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim compute_basis quotation, checked by script against its own policy's rule. Backward, each load-bearing sentence was walked to its binding: the month-counting sentences to `MONTHS`, now worded as the expression computes; each ladder paragraph to its ternary chain; "rounded to the nearest cent once at the end" to the single RND wrapping each result, the only intermediate roundings being those the rules state for a restored coverage month, for the arrears collected and for the rider premium met; "never less than nothing" to the MX(0, ...) guards; "the rider premium owing is the monthly rider premium multiplied by the coverage months of rider premium reckoned as owing" to the product in the withdrawal's offset; and "stops at the maximum out-of-pocket the line is capped against" to the MN in the root's result, which also fixes the moment the cap applies, after the share is worked out. Every window and status filter in an expression has its sentence, and no sentence is unclaimed.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and what the customer says: she wants the denied surgery restated; the published rule says a corrected liability is not fixed before the enrollment stands in force with no coverage end date, and the record shows it terminated; the restoration rule says such a coverage is restored only once no other election stands awaiting the transaction reply, and the record shows one at cms_transaction_pending; the charter reserves withdrawing an application to the member. Rosalind Ashby is seventy-five and telephones from 2135550394 mid-afternoon, with a letter from an ambulatory surgery centre in front of her and her reading glasses pushed up into her hair.
